title: Completing the Square to Find a Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Rewrite q(x) = x^2 - 6x + 11 in completed-square form, use it to prove q(x) >= 2 for all real x, and state the range of q.

steps.title: Complete the Square
steps.explanation: Half of the linear coefficient -6 is -3, and its square 9 is split out of the constant 11, leaving a perfect-square trinomial plus a residue of 2.
steps.why: The identity (x + p/2)^2 = x^2 + px + (p/2)^2 is exactly what the algebra performs in reverse.

steps.title: Bound the Square Below
steps.explanation: Any real number squared is nonnegative, so the squared term can never dip below zero no matter what x is chosen.
steps.why: Nonnegativity of squares is an order axiom of the reals: products of like-signed numbers are positive.

steps.title: Deduce the Global Minimum
steps.explanation: Adding 2 to a quantity that is at least 0 keeps it at least 2, and equality is actually attained at x = 3, so 2 is a true minimum rather than a mere bound.
steps.why: A lower bound that the function achieves is the minimum; the vertex (3, 2) is the parabola's lowest point.

steps.title: Read Off the Range
steps.explanation: As x moves away from 3 the square term grows without limit and q is continuous, so every value from 2 upward is taken exactly once on each side of the vertex.
steps.why: A continuous upward parabola attains every level above its minimum by the intermediate value property.
